εὑρίσκω.long: I find, learn, discover, especially after searching.
εὑρίσκω.der: a prolonged form of a primary , which (together with another cognate form) is used for it in all the tenses except the present and imperfect;
εὑρίσκω.as:
εὑρίσκω,
[in LXX chiefly for מצא, also for נשׂג hi., etc. ;]
to find, with or without previous search: absol., opp. to ζητέω, Mt 7:7, 8Lk 11:9, 10; c. acc., Mt 2:8, Mk 1:37, Ac 13:22, II Ti 1:17, al.; pass., οὐχ εὑ., of disappearance, He 11:5, Re 16:20, al.; γῆ κ. τὰ ἐν αὐτῇ ἔργα εὑρεθήσεται (for conjectures as to the meaning of this reading, v. Mayor, ICC, in l.), II Pe 3:10, WH, R, mg. Metaph., to find, find out by inquiry, learn, discover: Lk 19:48, Ac 4:21; αἰτίαν, Jo 18:38, Ac 13:28, al.; pass., Mt 1:18, Lk 17:18, Ro 7:10, I Co 4:2, Ga 2:17, I Pe 1:7, Re 5:4, al.; of attaining to the knowledge of God, εὑ. θεόν, Ac 17:27; pass., Ro 10:20(LXX). Mid., to find for oneself, gain, procure, obtain: c. acc. rei, λύτρωσιν, He 9:12; act. in same sense (so cl. poets, but not in Attic prose), Mt 10:3911:29, Lk 1:30, Ac 7:46, II Ti 1:18, al. (cf. ἀν-ευρίσκω).

εὐθύς.long: adj: (a) straight of direction, as opposed to crooked, (b) upright; adv: immediately.
εὐθύς.sd: straight, i.e. (literally) level, or (figuratively) true; adverbially (of time) at once
εὐθύς.kj: anon, by and by, forthwith, immediately, straightway
εὐθύς.as:
εὐθύς, -εῖα, -ύ
[in LXX chiefly for יָשַׁר ;]
1.straight, direct: τρίβοι, Mt 3:3, Mk 1:3, Lk 3:4(LXX); εἰς εὐθειας, (sc. ὁδούς), Lk 3:5; εὐ. ὐδός, fig., Ac 13:10, II Pe 2:15; as pr. name of a street, Ac 9:11.
2. In moral sense, straightforward, right: καρδία, Ac 8:21 (cf. Ps 7:1131 (32):11, al.).†

εὐδοκέω.long: I am well-pleased, think it good, am resolved.
εὐδοκέω.sd: to think well of, i.e. approve (an act); specially, to approbate (a person or thing)
εὐδοκέω.kj: think good, (be well) please(-d), be the good (have, take) pleasure, be willing
εὐδοκέω.as:
† εὐ-δοκέω, -ῶ
(on the derivation, v. BL, § 28, 6) [in LXX chiefly for רָצָה, also for אָבָה, חָפֵץ, etc. ;]
1. c. inf. (Polyb., al.), to be well pleased, to think it good, to give consent (so freq. in π. in legal docu­ments; Milligan, Th., 22 f.): Lk 12:32, Ro 15:26-27, I Co 1:21, Ga 1:15, Col 1:19, R, mg. (ICC, in l., but v. infr.), I Th 2:83:1; μᾶλλον εὐ., II Co 5:8; c. acc et inf. (Polyb., i, 8, 4), Col, l.c., R, txt. (Lft., in l).
2.to be well pleased or take pleasure with or in a person or thing;
(a) c. dat. (Polyb., al.; I Mac 1:43, I Es 4:39): II Th 2:12;
(b) as freq. in LXX,
(α) c. acc: Mt 12:13, He 10:5, 8(LXX);
β seq. ἐν (cf. Heb. רָצָה בְּ, Ps 149:4): Mt 3:1717:5, Mk 1:11, Lk 3:22 (on the tense, v. M, Pr., 134 f.; DCG, i,308 b), I Co 10:5, II Co 12:10, He 10:38(LXX);
(c) seq. εἰς: II Pe 1:17. (cf. συν-ευδοκέω, and v. Cremer, 213 f.; Field, Notes, 48 f.; DCG, i, 355a.)†

εὐθέως.sd: directly, i.e. at once or soon
εὐθέως.kj: anon, as soon as, forthwith, immediately, shortly, straightway
εὐθέως.as:
εὐθέως
adv.
(< εὐθύς), [in LXX: Jb 5:3 (פִּתְאֹם), Wi 5:12, I Mac 11:12, al. ;]
straightway, at once, directly: Ga 1:16, Ja 1:24, III Jo 14 (cf. Dalman, Words, 28 f.), Re 4:2, and freq. in Mt, Lk, Jo, Ac (in Mk, εὐθύς), q.v.)

εὐαγγέλιον.long: the good news of the coming of the Messiah, the gospel; the gen. after it expresses sometimes the giver (God), sometimes the subject (the Messiah, etc.), sometimes the human transmitter (an apostle).
εὐαγγέλιον.sd: a good message, i.e. the gospel
εὐαγγέλιον.as:
εὐαγγέλιον, -ου, τό
[in LXX for בְּשׂוֹרָה, בְּשׂרָה, II Ki 4:1018:2218:25 * ;]
1. in cl.,
(a)בְּשׂוֹרָה, a reward for good tidings (Hom.; pl., LXX, II Ki 4:10);
(b) in pl., εὐ. θύειν, to make a thank-offering for good tidings (Xen., al.).
2. Later (Luc., Plut., al.), good tidings, good news; in NT of the good tidings of the kingdom of God and of salvation through Christ, the gospel: Mk 1:15, Ac 15:7, Ro 1:16, Ga 2:2, I Th 2:4, al.; c. gen. obj., τ. βασιλείας, Mt 4:23; τ. Χριστοῦ, Ro 15:19, al.; τ. κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ, II Th 1:8; τ. υἱοῦ τ. θεοῦ, Ro 1:9; τ. δόξης τ. μακαρίου θεοῦ, I Ti 1:11; τ. δόξης τ. Χριστοῦ, II Co 4:4; of the author, τ. θεοῦ, Ro 15:16, al.; of the teacher, ἡμῶν, Ro 2:16, II Co 4:3, I Th 1:5, II Ti 2:8; of the taught, τ. περιτομῆς, τ. ἀκροβυστίας, Ga 2:7; ἡ ἀλήθεια τοῦ εὐ., Ga 2:5, 14Col 1:5; ἡ ἐλπὶς (πίστις) τοῦ εὐ., Col 1:23, Phl 1:27 (v. Cremer, 31 ff.; and on the later eccl. use of the word„ M, Th., 143 f.)

εὐνοέω.sd: to be well- minded, i.e. reconcile
εὐνοέω.der: from a compound of G2095 (εὖ) and G3563 (νοῦς);
εὐνοέω.as:
εὐ-νοέω, -ῶ
(< εὔνοος, friendly), [in LXX: Es 8:13 Bא1, Da LXX 2:43, III Mac 7:11 * ;]
to be favourable, kindly disposed: c. dat., Mt 5:25.†

εὐρύχωρος.as:
εὐρύ-χωρος, -ον
(< εὐρύς, broad + χώρα), [in LXX for רָחַב ni., and cognate forms (Is 30:23, al.), exc. II Ch 18:9 (גֹּרֶן ;]
spacious, broad: Mt 7:13.†

εὐκοπώτερος.sd: better for toil, i.e. more facile
εὐκοπώτερος.der: comparative of a compound of G2095 (εὖ) and G2873 (κόπος);
εὐκοπώτερος.as:
**† εὔ-κοπος, -ον
[in LXX: Si 22:15, I Mac 3:18 * ;]
with easy labour, easy: compar., -ώτερόν ἐστι, c. inf., Mt 9:5, Mk 2:9, Lk 5:23; c. acc et inf., Mt 19:24, Mk 10:25, Lk 16:1718:25 (Polyb.; the adv. -ως occurs in Aristoph., Fr., 615).†

εὐαγγελίζω.g: I bring good news, preach good tidings
εὐαγγελίζω.long: I bring good news, preach good tidings, with or without an object, expressing either the persons who receive the good news or the good news itself (the good news being sometimes expressed as a person).
εὐαγγελίζω.sd: to announce good news ("evangelize") especially the gospel
εὐαγγελίζω.kj: declare, bring (declare, show) glad (good) tidings, preach (the gospel)
εὐαγγελίζω.as:
εὐαγγελίζω
[in LXX for בָּשַׂר pi., hith.; for good news in general: I Ki 31:9, al.; of God's loving kindness, Ps 39 (40):1095 (96):2, and esp. of Messianic blessings, Is 40:960:6, al. ;]
to bring or announce glad tidings;
1. act. (only in late writers): c. acc pers., Re 10:7; seq. ἐπί, c. acc pers., Re 14:6; pass., of things, to be proclaimed as glad tidings: Lk 16:16, Ga 1:11, I Pe 1:25; impers., I Pe 4:6; of persons, to have glad tidings proclaimed to one: Mt 11:5, Lk 7:22, He 4:2, 6
2. Depon. mid. (cl.), to proclaim glad tidings, in NT esp. of the Christian message of salvation: absol., Lk 9:6, Ro 15:20, al.; c. dat. pers., Lk 4:18(LXX), Ro 1:15, al.; in same sense c. acc pers. (not cl.), Lk 3:18, Ac 16:10, Ga 1:9, I Pe 1:12; c. acc rei, εἰρήνην, Ac 10:36, Ro 10:15(LXX); τ, βασιλείαν τ. θεοῦ, Lk 8:1; c. dat. pers., Lk 1:194:43, Eph 2:173:8; αὐτῷ τ. Ἰησοῦν, Ac 8:3517:18; c. dupl. acc, Ac 13:32; c. acc pers. et inf., Ac 14:15; τ. κώμας (πολεῖς), Ac 8:25, 4014:21 (cf. προ-ευαγγελίζομαι)

εὐδοκία.long: (a) good-will (good-pleasure), favor, feeling of complacency of God to man, (b) good-pleasure, satisfaction, happiness, delight of men.
εὐδοκία.sd: satisfaction, i.e. (subjectively) delight, or (objectively) kindness, wish, purpose
εὐδοκία.kj: desire, good pleasure (will), X seem good
εὐδοκία.der: from a presumed compound of G2095 (εὖ) and the base of G1380 (δοκέω);
εὐδοκία.as:
† εὐδοκία, -ας, ἡ
(< εὐδοκέω, q.v.), [in LXX: Ps 5:12, al. (רָצוֹן), freq. in Si; in Inscr. (I.G., 5960), LXX, and NT = εὐδόκησις (Diod.) ;]
good pleasure, good-will, satisfaction, approval: Mt 11:26, Lk 10:21, Ro 10:1, Eph 1:5, 9, Phl 1:152:13; c. gen. obj., II Th 1:11 (v. Milligan, in l); ἐν ἀνθρώποις εὐδοκία, Rec., R, mg., WH, mg. (v. Field, Notes, 48 f.), Lk 2:14; -ας, Lk, l.c., R, txt., WH, txt. (v. ICC, in l; WH, App., in l).†

εὐλογέω.long: (lit: I speak well of) I bless; pass: I am blessed.
εὐλογέω.sd: to speak well of, i.e. (religiously) to bless (thank or invoke a benediction upon, prosper)
εὐλογέω.der: from a compound of G2095 (εὖ) and G3056 (λόγος);
εὐλογέω.as:
εὐλογέω, -ῶ
[in LXX chiefly for בָּרַךְ pi. ;]
1.to speak well of, praise (cl.; LXX De 8:10, al.): τ. θεόν, Lk 1:642:2824:51, 53 (αἰνοῦντες, T, WH, mg.), Ja 3:9; absol., to give praise, Mt 14:1926:26 (v. Swete on Mk 14:22), Mk 6:4114:22 (v. Swete, in l.), Lk 24:30, I Co 14:16.
2. As in LXX (= בָּרַךְ pi.);
(a)to bless, invoke blessings on (Ge 24:60, Nu 23:20, al.): absol., I Co 4:12, I Pe 3:9; c. acc pers., Lk 2:346:2824:50, 51, Ro 12:14, He 7:1, 6, 711:20, 21; εὐλογημένος (= בָּרוּךְ; v. Lft., Notes, 310; DCG, i, 189), blessed, Mt 21:923:39(LXX), Mk 11:9, 10, Lk 13:3519:38(LXX), Jo 12:13; c. acc rei, Mk 8:7, Lk 9:16, I Co 10:16;
(b) with God as subject (Ps 44:3, al.), to bless, prosper, bestow blessings on: c. acc pers., Ac 3:26, Ga 3:9, Eph 1:3 (Lft., Notes, 311), He 6:14; εὐλογημένος, Lk 1:28 (WH, txt., R, txt., omit) ib. 42; εὐλογημένοι τ. πατρός (cf. Is 61:9), Mt 25:34; pass. Ac 3:25 (cf. ἐν-, κατ-ευλογέω).†
SYN.: v.s. αἰνέω, and cf. DCG, i, 189, 211; Cremer, 766

εὐχαριστέω.long: I thank, give thanks; pass. 3 sing: is received with thanks.
εὐχαριστέω.sd: to be grateful, i.e. (actively) to express gratitude (towards); specially, to say grace at a meal
εὐχαριστέω.as:
** εὐχαριστέω, -ῶ
[in LXX: Jth 8:25Wi 18:2, II Mac 1:1110:7 A II Mac 12:31 R, III Mac 7:16 * ;]
to be thankful, give thanks (chiefly in late writers and Inscr.; cf. Milligan, Th., 5; Ellic. on Col 1:12; Lft., Notes, 9): Ro 1:21, I Co 14:17, I Th 5:18; of giving thanks before meat, Mt 15:3626:27, Mk 8:614:23, Lk 22:17, 19, Jo 6:11, 23, I Co 11:24; c. dat. pens., τ. θεῷ, Lk 17:16, Ac 27:3528:15, Ro 14:616:4, I Co 14:18, Phl 1:3, Col 1:3, 12, Phm 4; seq. διὰ Ἰ. Χριστοῦ, Ro 1:87:25, R, WH, mg., Col 3:17; ἐν ὀνόματι Χρ., Eph 5:20; seq. περί, I Th 1:2, II Th 1:3; ὅτι, Ro 1:8, II Th 2:13; ἐπι, c. dat. rei, I Co 1:4; ὐπέρ, I Co 10:30, Eph 1:165:20; ὅτι, Lk 18:11, Jo 11:41, I Co 1:14, I Th 2:13, Re 11:17; pass. (Deiss., BS, 122 f.), II Co 1:11.†
SYN.: v.s. αἰνέω; and cf. Cremer, 903 f

εὐδία.sd: a clear sky, i.e. fine weather
εὐδία.der: feminine from G2095 (εὖ) and the alternate of G2203 (Ζεύς) (as the god of the weather);
εὐδία.as:
** εὐδία, -ας, ἡ
[in LXX: Si 3:15 * ;] (< εὔδιος, calm)
fair weather: Mt 16:2 (Rec., R, txt.).†

εὐνοῦχος.g: a eunuch, keeper of the bed-chamber
εὐνοῦχος.long: (a) a chamberlain, keeper of the bed-chamber of an eastern potentate, eunuch, (b) a eunuch, castrated person, or one who voluntarily abstains from marriage.
εὐνοῦχος.sd: a castrated person (such being employed in Oriental bed-chambers); by extension an impotent or unmarried man; by implication, a chamberlain (state-officer)
εὐνοῦχος.as:
εὐνοῦχος, -ου, ὁ
(i.e. ὁ τὴν εὐνὴν (bed) ἔχων), [in LXX for סָרִיס (perhaps not of necessity an actual eunuch; DB, s.v.), Ge 39:1, al., Wi 3:14, Si 20:430:20 ;]
an emasculated man, a eunuch: Mt 19:12; one such holding, as was common, high office, as of chamberlain, at court, Ac 8:27, 34, 36, 38, 39; metaph., of one naturally incapacitated for or volun­tarily abstaining from wedlock, Mt 19:12.†

εὐνουχίζω.long: I make into a eunuch, emasculate, castrate.
εὐνουχίζω.as:
*† εὐνουχίζω
(< εὐνοῦχος),
to make a eunuch of, castrate: pass., Mt 19:12; metaph., εὐ. έαυτόν, ib.†

εὐώνυμος.long: (lit: well-named, to avoid the evil omen attaching to the left), on the left-hand side, left.
εὐώνυμος.sd: properly, well-named (good-omened), i.e. the left (which was the lucky side among the pagan Greeks); neuter as adverbial, at the left hand
εὐώνυμος.as:
εὐώνυμος, -ον
(εὖ, ὄνομα), [in LXX chiefly for שְׂמאׄל ;]
1.of good name or omen
2. Euphemistic for ἀριστερός, left: Ac 21:3, Re 10:2; ἐξ εὐωνύμων, on the left: Mt 20:21, 2325:33, 4127:38, Mk 10:4015:27.†

εὖ.long: well, well done, good, rightly; also used as an exclamation.
εὖ.as:
εὖ
adv.
(prop. neuter of old Epic ἐΰς, good, noble) [in LXX, εὖ γίγνεσθαι, εὖ ποιεῖν (יָטַב) ;]
well: εὖ γιν., Eph 6:3(LXX); εὖ ποιεῖν, c. dat. (cf. Si 12:1-2), to do good, Mk 14:7 (where Nestle suggests εὐποιεῖν, q.v.); εὖ πράσστειν, to fare well, Ac 15:29; in replies (= εὖγε), good! well done!Mt 25:21, 23Lk 19:17 (εὖγε, WH, txt.).†

εὐκαιρία.as:
εὐκαιρία, -ας, ἡ
(< εὔκαιρος), [in LXX: Ps 9:10 (v. Soph., Lex., s.v.) 9:22 (10:1)144 (145):15 (עֵת), Si 38:24, I Mac 11:42 * ;]
fitting time, opportunity: seq. ἵνα, Mt 26:16; τοῦ, c. inf., Lk 22:6.†

εὔκαιρος.long: opportune, timely, suitable; perhaps sometimes: holiday, festival.
εὔκαιρος.as:
εὔ-καιρος, -ον
[in LXX: Ps 103 (104):27 (עֵת), II Mac 14:2915:20, 21, III Mac 4:115:44 * ;]
timely, seasonable, suitable (Cremer, 740): ἡμέρα, Mk 6:21 (or empty, as in Byz. and MGr.; v. MM, Exp., xiv); βοήθεια, He 4:16.†

εὐκαιρέω.g: I have a good opportunity, have leisure
εὐκαιρέω.long: I have a good (favorable) opportunity, have leisure; I devote my leisure to.
εὐκαιρέω.sd: to have good time, i.e. opportunity or leisure
εὐκαιρέω.as:
*† εὐκαιρέω, -ῶ
(= cl., εὖ σχολῆς ἔχειν; used by Polyb. and Philo; cf. Rutherford, NPhr. 205; MM, Exp., xiv),
to have leisure or opportunityI Co 16:12; c. inf., Mk 6:31; seq. εἰς, to devote one's leisure to, Ac 17:21.†

εὐκαίρως.as:
** εὐκαίρως
adv.,
[in LXX: Si 18:22 * ;]
seasonably, in season: Mk 14:11; opp. to ἀκ- (Kühner3, iv, 346 d), II Ti 4:2.†

εὐλογητός.long: (used only of God), blessed (as entitled to receive blessing from man), worthy of praise.
εὐλογητός.as:
† εὐλογητός, -όν
(< εὐλογέω), [in LXX chiefly for בָּרוּךְ ;]
blessed;
(a) of men (Ge 12:2 A, De 7:14, Jg 17:2 B, Ru 2:20, I Ki 15:13);
(b) of God (Lft., Notes, 310 f.), as chiefly in LXX (Ge 9:26, Ex 17:10, Ps 17 (18):46, al.): Lk 1:68, Ro 1:259:5 (ICC, in l), II Co 1:311:31, Eph 1:3, I Pe 1:3; absol., ὁ εὐλογητός (Dalman, Words, 200; JThS, v, 453), Mk 14:61 (Cremer, 769).†

εὐσχήμων.long: (a) comely, seemly, decorous, (b) of honorable position (in society), wealthy, influential.
εὐσχήμων.as:
εὐσχήμων, -ον
(εὖ, σχῆμα), [in LXX: Pr 11:25 * ;]
1.elegant, graceful, comely (Eur., Plat., al.): τὰ εὐ. ἡμῶν (opp. to τὰ ἀσχ- ἡμ-), I Co 12:24; in moral sense, seemly, becoming, I Co 7:35.
2. Also in late Gk. (v. Swete, Mk., l.c.; MM, Exp., xiv), wealthy, influential (RV, of honourable estate): Mk 15:43, Ac 13:5017:12.†

εὐλαβής.long: (lit: handling well, hence) cautious, circumspect; hence: God-fearing, pious.
εὐλαβής.as:
εὐλαβής, -ές
(< εὖ, λαβεῖν), [in LXX: Mi 7:2 AB2 (חָסִיד); εὐ. ποιεῖν, Le 15:31 (נָזַר hi.), Si 11:7א2* ;]
1.cautious, circumspect.
2.devout, religious, reverent: Ac 2:58:222:12; δίκαιος καὶ εὐ., Lk 2:25.†

εὔθετος.der: from G2095 (εὖ) and a derivative of G5087 (τίθημι);
εὔθετος.as:
εὔ-θετος, -ον
(< τίθημι), [in LXX: Ps 31 (32):6 (מָצָא), Da TH Su 1:15* ;]
ready for use, fit: of things, c. dat., He 6:7; seq. εἰς, Lk 14:35; of persons, c. dat., Lk 9:62 (for rabbinic parallels, v. Dalman, Words, 119 f.).†

εὐφορέω.g: I bear well, bring a good harvest
εὐφορέω.long: I bear well, bring a good harvest, yield abundantly.
εὐφορέω.sd: to bear well, i.e. be fertile

εὐφραίνω.g: I cheer, am glad, make merry
εὐφραίνω.long: I cheer, make glad; generally mid. or pass: I am glad, make merry, revel, feast.
εὐφραίνω.sd: to put (middle voice or passively, be) in a good frame of mind, i.e. rejoice
εὐφραίνω.kj: fare, make glad, be (make) merry, rejoice
εὐφραίνω.as:
εὐφραίνω
[in LXX chiefly for שָׂמַח, qal, pi. ;]
to cheer, gladden: c. acc pers., opp. to λυπεῖν, II Co 2:2. Pass., to be happy, rejoice, make merry: Lk 15:32, Ac 2:26(LXX)Ro 15:10(LXX), Ga 4:27(LXX), Re 11:1012:12; seq. ἐν, Ac 7:41; ἐπί c. dat., Re 18:20; of merry-making at a feast (III Ki 4:20; cf. Kennedy, Sources, 155; Field, Notes, 69 f.), Lk 12:1915:23, 24, 29(LXX) (λαμπρῶς) Lk 16:19.†

εὐγενής.long: (a) of noble birth, of high birth, (b) noble in nature.
εὐγενής.sd: well born, i.e. (literally) high in rank, or (figuratively) generous
εὐγενής.as:
εὐγενής, -ές
(< εὖ, γένος), [in LXX: Jb 1:3 (גָּדוֹל), II Mac 10:13 R, IV Mac 6:59:13, 23, 2710:3, 15 * ;]
1.well born, of noble race: Lk 19:12, I Co 1:26.
2.noble-minded: compar., -έστερος, Ac 17:11.†

εὖγε.long: well, well done, good, rightly; also used as an exclamation.
εὖγε.as:
εὖ-γε
adv.
in replies, well! good! well done!: Lk 19:17 (WH for Rec. εὖ, q.v.).†

εὐεργέτης.sd: a worker of good, i.e. (specially) a philanthropist
εὐεργέτης.der: from G2095 (εὖ) and the base of G2041 (ἔργον);
εὐεργέτης.as:
** εὐεργέτης, -ου, ὁ
[in LXX: Es 8:13, Wi 19:14, II Mac 4:2, III Mac 3:196:24 * ;]
a benefactor: Lk 22:25 (for contemp. usage, v. Deiss., LAE, 248).†

εὐτόνως.sd: in a well-strung manner, i.e. (figuratively) intensely (in a good sense, cogently; in a bad one, fiercely)
εὐτόνως.der: adverb from a compound of G2095 (εὖ) and a derivative of (to stretch);
εὐτόνως.as:
εὐτόνως
adv.
(< εὖ, τείνω), [in LXX forבַּשּׁוֹפָרוֹתJos 6:7(8) * ;]
vigorously, vehemently: Lk 23:10, Ac 18:28.†

εὐθύνω.long: (a) I make straight (of the direction, not the surface, of a road), (b) I guide, steer.
εὐθύνω.as:
εὐθύνω
(< εὐθύς), [in LXX: Nu 22:23, Jos 24:23 (נָטָה hi.), Jg 14:7, I Ki 18:20, 26 (יָשַׁר) Pr 20:24, Si 2:2, 6, al. ;]
1.to direct: Ja 3:4.
2.to make straight: Jo 1:23 (LXX, ἑτοιμάσατε).†

εὐφροσύνη.as:
εὐφροσύνη, -ης, ἡ
(< εὔφρων, cheerful) [in LXX chiefly for שִׂמְחָה ;]
rejoicing, gladness: Ac 2:28(LXX)14:17.†

εὐσέβεια.as:
εὐ-σέβεια, -ας, ἡ
(< εὐσεβής, q.v.), [in LXX: Pr 1:7, Is 33:6 (יִרְאָה), Pr 13:11 (aliter in Heb.), Is 11:2 (יְהֹוָהיִרְאָה), I Es 1:23, Wi 10:12, Si 49:3, and very freq. in IV Mac ;]
1.piety, reverence (towards parents and others).
2.piety towards God, godliness: Ac 3:12, I Ti 2:24:7, 86:5, 6, 11, II Pe 1:3, 6, 7,; τὸ τῆς εὐ. μυστήριον, I Ti 3:16; ἡ κατ’ εὐ. διδασκαλία, I Ti 6:3; ἡ ἀλήθεια ἡ κατ' εὐ., Tit 1:1; μόρφωσις εὐσεβείας, II Ti 3:5; pl. (v. Bl., § 32, 6; Mayor on Ja 2:1), II Pe 3:11 (on the use of εὐ. and cognates in Past. Epp., v. CGT, on I Ti 2:2; cf. also Cremer, 524).†

εὐεργεσία.long: good action, well-doing, benefiting, kind service.
εὐεργεσία.as:
εὐεργεσία, -ας, ἡ
(< εὐεργέτης), [in LXX: Ps 77 (78):11 (עֲלִילָה), Wi 16:11, 24, II Mac 6:139:26, IV Mac 8:17 * ;]
a good deed, kindness, benefit: I Ti 6:2; c. gen. pers. (εὐ. πόλεως, Plat., leg., 805b), Ac 4:9,†

εὐσεβής.as:
εὐσεβής, -ές
(< εὖ, σέβομαι), [in LXX: Pr 12:12, Is 24:1626:7 (צַדִּיק), Mi 7:2 (חָסִיד), Is 32:8 (נָדִיב), and freq. in Si and IV Mac;]
pious, godly, devout: Ac 10:2, 7, II Pe 2:9.†
SYN.: θεοσεβής, θρῆσκος (v. Tr., Syn., § xlviii; DB, ii, 221 f.; Cremer, 524 f., 858)

εὐεργετέω.long: I do good deeds, perform kind service, benefit.
εὐεργετέω.as:
εὐεργετέω, -ῶ
(< εὐεργέτης), [in LXX: Ps 12 (13):6 (גָּמַל), Wi 3:5, al. ;]
to do good, bestow benefit: Ac 10:38.†

εὐπορέομαι.long: I have means, am prosperous, enjoy plenty.
εὐπορέομαι.sd: (intransitively) to be good for passing through, i.e. (figuratively) have pecuniary means
εὐπορέομαι.der: from a compound of G2090 (ἑτοιμάζω) and the base of G4197 (πορεία);
εὐπορέομαι.as:
εὐ-πορέω, -ῶ
(< εὔτορος, well provided for) [in LXX: Le 25:26, 49נָשַׂג hi.), ib. 28 (v.l.), Wi 10:10 * ;]
to prosper, be well off: Ac 11:29.†

εὐθυδρομέω.sd: to lay a straight course, i.e. sail direct
εὐθυδρομέω.as:
*† εὐθυδρομέω, -ῶ
of ships, to run a straight course (Philo): Ac 16:1121:1.†

εὐσεβέω.long: I am dutiful, pious, show piety towards, worship.
εὐσεβέω.sd: to be pious, i.e. (towards God) to worship, or (towards parents) to respect (support)
εὐσεβέω.as:
** εὐ-σεβέω, -ῶ
(< εὐσεβής, q.v.), [in LXX: Da LXX Su 1:64, IV Mac 9:6אR, IV Mac 11:5, 8, 23 18:2 * ;]
to reverence, show piety towards; c. acc (else­where more freq. seq. εἰς., περί, πρός): οἶκον, I Ti 5:4; θεόν, Ac 17:23 (Cremer, 525).†

εὐχή.long: a prayer comprising a vow; a prayer, vow.
εὐχή.sd: properly, a wish, expressed as a petition to God, or in votive obligation
εὐχή.as:
εὐχή, -ῆς, ἡ
(< εὔχομαι), [in LXX chiefly for נֵדֶר ;]
1.a prayer: Ja 5:15.
2.a vow: Ac 18:1821:23.†
SYN.: v.s. δέησις

εὐπορία.as:
εὐ-πορία, -ας, ἡ
(< εὔπορος), [in LXX for חַיִל, IV Ki 25:10 A (freq. in Aq.)* ;]
1.facility.
2.plenty, wealth: Ac 19:25.†

Εὔτυχος.long: Eutychus, a young hearer of Paul at Troas.
Εὔτυχος.sd: well- fated, i.e. fortunate; Eutychus, a young man
Εὔτυχος.der: from G2095 (εὖ) and a derivative of G5177 (τυγχάνω);
Εὔτυχος.as:
Εὔτυχος, -ου, ὁ
(εὖ, τυχή),
Eutychus, a young man: Ac 20:9.†

εὐαγγελιστής.g: an evangelist, bearer of good tidings
εὐαγγελιστής.long: an evangelist, a missionary, bearer of good tidings.
εὐαγγελιστής.as:
*† εὐαγγελιστής, -οῦ, ὁ
an evangelist;
(a) in NT, a preacher of the gospel: Ac 21:8, Eph 4:11, II Ti 4:5;
(b) later, a writer of a gospel (eccl.).†

εὐχαριστία.long: thankfulness, gratitude; giving of thanks, thanksgiving.
εὐχαριστία.sd: gratitude; actively, grateful language (to God, as an act of worship)
εὐχαριστία.as:
** εὐχαριστία, -ας, ἡ
(< εὐχάριστος), [in LXX: Es 8:13, Wi 16:28, Si 37:11, II Mac 2:27 * ;]
1.thankfulness, gratitude (Polyb.; Es, Si, II Mac, ll. c.): Ac 24:3.
2.giving of thanks, thanksgiving (so in π. and Inscr.; M, Th., 41 f.): I Co 14:16, II Co 4:15, Eph 5:4, Phl 4:6, Col 2:74:2, I Th 3:9, I Ti 4:3, 4, Re 4:97:12; c. dat. pers., II Co 9:11 (cf. τ.θεοῦ, Wis, l.c.); pl., II Co 9:12, I Ti 2:1 (Cremer, 904).†

εὔχομαι.sd: to wish; by implication, to pray to God
εὔχομαι.der: middle voice of a primary verb;
εὔχομαι.as:
εὔχομαι
[in LXX chiefly for נָדַד, also for עָתַר hi., etc. ;]
to pray: c. acc rei, II Co 13:9; c. dat. pers., τ. θεῷ, Ac 26:29; seq. πρὸς τ. θεόν, II Co 13:7; c. acc et inf., Ac 27:29, III Jo 2; seq. ὑπέρ, Ja 5:16; ηὐχόμην εἶναι (on impf. here, v. ICC, in l., Lft., Phm 13), Ro 9:3 (Cremer, 718).†

εὐρακύλων.sd: a storm from the East (or southeast), i.e. (in modern phrase) a Levanter
εὐρακύλων.as:
† Εὐρ-ακύλων (Rec. εὐροκλύδων, q.v.), -ωνος
(< Εὖρος, the East wind, and Lat. Aquilo; Vg., Euroaquilo),
the Euraquilo, a N.E. wind (i.e. between Eurus and Aquilo): Ac 27:14.†

εὐθυμέω.long: I keep up spirit, am cheerful, am of good courage.
εὐθυμέω.sd: to cheer up, i.e. (intransitively) be cheerful; neuter comparative (adverbially) more cheerfully
εὐθυμέω.as:
** εὐθυμέω, -ῶ
(< ὔθυμος), [in Sm.: Ps 31 (32):11, Pr 15:15 * ;]
1. trans., to make cheerful (Æsch.).
2. Intrans. (Eur., Plut.; so mid. in Xen., Plat.), to be of good cheer: Ac 27:22, 25, Ja 5:13.†

εὔθυμος.kj: of good cheer, the more cheerfully
εὔθυμος.as:
** εὔ-θυμος, -ον
[in LXX: II Mac 11:26 * ;]
1.kind (Hom.).
2.of good cheer (Æsch., al.): Ac 27:36.†

εὐοδόομαι.g: I cause to prosper, have a happy journey
εὐοδόομαι.long: I cause to prosper, pass: I have a happy (successful) journey, hence: I prosper.
εὐοδόομαι.sd: to help on the road, i.e. (passively) succeed in reaching; figuratively, to succeed in business affairs
εὐοδόομαι.der: from a compound of G2095 (εὖ) and G3598 (ὁδός);
εὐοδόομαι.as:
εὐ-οδόω, -ῶ
(< ὁδός), [in LXX chiefly for צָלַח hi. ;]
to help on one's way (Soph., al.). Pass., to have a prosperous journey; metaph. (Hdt., al.), to prosper, be prospered, be successful: III Jo 2, Ro 1:10, I Co 16:2 (on the tense, v. M, Pr., 54; ICC, in l.).†

εὐάρεστος.as:
**† εὐ-άρεστος, -ον
[in LXX: Wi 4:109:10 * ;]
well-pleasing, acceptable: Ro 12:2; c. dat. pers., Ro 12:114:18, II Co 5:9, Eph 5:10, Phl 4:18; id. seq. ἐν, Tit 2:9 (κυρίῳ), Col 3:20; ἐνώπιον, He 13:21 (for ex. in Inser., v. Deiss., BS, 215).†

εὐσχημόνως.as:
* εὐσχημόνως
adv.
(< εὐσχήμων),
decorously, becomingly: I Co 14:40; περιπατεῖν, Ro 13:13, I Th 4:12.†

εὐπρόσδεκτος.der: from G2095 (εὖ) and a derivative of G4327 (προσδέχομαι);
εὐπρόσδεκτος.as:
† εὐ-πρόσ-δεκτος, -ον
(< εὖ, προσδέχομαι)
more usual than δέκτος, q.v., acceptable: Ro 15:16, 31, II Co 6:28:12, I Pe 2:5.†

εὐλογία.sd: fine speaking, i.e. elegance of language; commendation ("eulogy"), i.e. (reverentially) adoration; religiously, benediction; by implication, consecration; by extension, benefit or largess
εὐλογία.kj: blessing (a matter of) bounty (X -tifully), fair speech
εὐλογία.as:
εὐλογία, -ας, ἡ
[in LXX chiefly for בְּרָכָה ;]
1.fair speaking, flattering speech: χρηστολογίας καὶ εὐ., Ro 16:18.
2.praise: of God (as in late Inscr.; LS, s.v.) and Christ, Re 5:12, 137:12
3. In LXX and NT: blessing, benediction;
(a) the act of blessing: I Co 10:16, He 12:17, Ja 3:10;
(b) concrete, a blessing: Ro 15:29, II Co 9:5, 6, Ga 3:14, Eph 1:3, He 6:7, I Pe 3:9 (cf. De 11:26, Si 7:32, al.).†

εὐπάρεδρον.sd: sitting well towards, i.e. (figuratively) assiduous (neuter, diligent service)
εὐπάρεδρον.der: from G2095 (εὖ) and the same as G4332 (προσεδρεύω);
εὐπάρεδρον.as:
*† εὐ-πρόσ-εδρος, -ον
Rec. for εὐπάρεδρος, q.v.: I Co 7:35.†

εὐσχημοσύνη.as:
** εὐσχημοσύνη
(< εὐσχήμων), [in LXX: IV Mac 6:2 * ;]
seemliness, comeliness: I Co 12:23.†

εὔσημος.long: with clear meaning, intelligible, clear to the understanding.
εὔσημος.der: from G2095 (εὖ) and the base of G4591 (σημαίνω);
εὔσημος.as:
εὔσημος, -ον
(< εὖ + οῆμα, a sign) [in LXX for כֶּסֶא, Ps 80 (81):3 (-ως, Da LXX 2:19)* ;]
1.conspicuous (cf. Ps, l.c.).
2.clear to the understanding, distinct: I Co 14:9.†

εὐωδία.der: from a compound of G2095 (εὖ) and a derivative of G3605 (ὄζω);
εὐωδία.as:
εὐωδία, -ας, ἡ
(< εὐώδης, fragrant; < ὄζω) [in LXX for נִיחֹחַ, Ge 8:21, al. (ὀσμὴ εὐωδίας); Si 20:924:15, al. ;]
fragrance: metaph., Χριστοῦ εὐ,., II Co 2:15; ὀσμὴ εὐωδίας (a metaphor of sacrifice, most freq. in Pent. and Ez.), Eph 5:2, Phl 4:18.†

εὐφημία.as:
** εὐφημία, -ας, ἡ
(< εὔφημος), [in Sm.: Ps 41 (42):546 (47):299 (100):2125 (126):2 * ;]
good report, praise: opp. to δυσφημία, II Co 6:8.†

Εὕα.long: Eve, the first woman; wife of first man Adam.
Εὕα.sd: Eua (or Eva, i.e. Chavvah), the first woman
Εὕα.as:
Εὔα (WH, Εὕα, § 408; Rec. Εὖα; S (in I Ti), Εὕα), -ας, ἡ (Heb. חַוָּה, Ge 3:20),
Eve, wife of Adam: II Co 11:3, I Ti 2:13.†

εὐπροσωπέω.g: I make a fair outward appearance
εὐπροσωπέω.long: I look well, make a fair show (a good outward appearance, and so win good opinion).
εὐπροσωπέω.sd: to be of good countenance, i.e. (figuratively) to make a display
εὐπροσωπέω.der: from a compound of G2095 (εὖ) and G4383 (πρόσωπον);
εὐπροσωπέω.as:
**† εὐ-προσωπέω, -ῶ
(< εὐπρόσωπος, fair of face), [in Al.: Ps 140 (141):6, v.l. for -ίζω* ;]
to look well, make a fair show: metaph. (as in π.; v. Deiss., LAE, 96), Ga 6:12.†

εὔσπλαγχνος.as:
** εὔσπλαγχνος, -ον
(εὖ, σπλάγχνον, q.v.), [in Pr Ma 7 (Camb. Manual LXX, iii, 825) ;]
1. in Hippocr., as medical term (LS, s.v.).
2. Metaph. (cf. εὐσιλαγχνία, Eurip., Rhes., 192), in NT, tenderhearted, compassionate: Eph 4:32, I Pe 3:8.†

εὐτραπελία.sd: witticism, i.e. (in a vulgar sense) ribaldry
εὐτραπελία.der: from a compound of G2095 (εὖ) and a derivative of the base of G5157 (τροπή) (meaning well-turned, i.e. ready at repartee, jocose);
εὐτραπελία.as:
* εὐτραπελία, -ας, ἡ
(< εὖ, τρέπω),
1.versatility, wit, facetiousness (Hippocr., Plat., al.).
2. = βωμολογία, coarse jesting, ribaldry (Abbott, Essays, 93): Eph 5:4.†
SYN.: μωρολογία, v. Tr., Syn., § xxxiv

εὔνοια.as:
εὔνοια, -ας, ἡ
(< εὔνοος), [in LXX: Es 2:23, al. ;]
goodwill: Eph 6:7 (of slaves; cf. MM, Exp., xiv).†

εὐψυχέω.sd: to be in good spirits, i.e. feel encouraged
εὐψυχέω.der: from a compound of G2095 (εὖ) and G5590 (ψυχή);
εὐψυχέω.as:
*† εὐψυχέω, -ῶ
(< εὔψυχος, courageous),
to be of good courage: Phl 2:19.†

Εὐοδία.long: Euodia, or rather Euhodia, a Christian woman of Philippi.
Εὐοδία.sd: fine travelling; Euodia, a Christian woman
Εὐοδία.as:
Εὐοδία (Rec. -ωδία), -ας, ἡ
Euodia (not as AV, Euodias), a Christian woman: Phl 4:2.†

εὔφημος.g: well reported of, spoken in a kindly spirit
εὔφημος.long: well reported of, spoken in a kindly spirit, laudable, reputable.
εὔφημος.as:
εὔφημος, -ον
(εὖ, φήμη), [in Sm.: Ps 62 (63):6 ;]
primarily, utter­ing words or sounds of good omen, hence,
1.avoiding ill-omened words, religiously silent.
2.fair-sounding, auspicious (R, mg., gracious): Phl 4:8.†

εὐχάριστος.der: from G2095 (εὖ) and a derivative of G5483 (χαρίζομαι);
εὐχάριστος.as:
εὐχάριστος, -ον
(< εὖ, χαρίζομαι), [in LXX for חֵן, Pr 11:16 * ;]
1. = εὔχαρις, winning, gracious, agreeable (Pr, l.c.).
2.grateful, thankful: Col 3:15.†

εὐμετάδοτος.long: willingly sharing, ready to impart, generous.
εὐμετάδοτος.der: from G2095 (εὖ) and a presumed derivative of G3330 (μεταδίδωμι);
εὐμετάδοτος.as:
*† εὐ-μετά-δοτος, -ον
(< εὖ, μεταδιδωμι),
ready to impart: assoc. with κοινωνικός (for the distinction bet. the two, v. Field, Notes, 213; CGT, in l.), I Ti 6:18.†

Εὐνίκη.as:
Εὐνίκη (Rec. -νείκη), -ης,
Eunice, Timothy's mother: II Ti 1:5.†

εὔχρηστος.as:
εὔ-χρηστος, -ον
(εὖ, χράομαι), [in LXX: Pr 31:13 (חֵפֶץ), Wi 13:13 * ;]
useful, serviceable: c. dat. pers., II Ti 2:21; id. seq. εἰς, c. dat. rei, II Ti 4:11; opp. to ἄχρηστος, Phm 11.†

εὐσεβῶς.as:
** εὐσεβῶς
adv.,
[in LXX: IV Mac 7:21 * ;]
piously, religiously: II Ti 3:12, Tit 2:12.†

Εὔβουλος.long: Eubulus, a Christian with Paul in Rome.
Εὔβουλος.as:
Εὔβουλος, -ου, ὁ.
Eubulus, a Christian: II Ti 4:21.†

εὐθύτης.as:
εὐθύτης, -ητος, ἡ
(< εὐθύς), [in LXX chiefly for יֹשֶׁר, מִישׁוֹר and cognate forms ;]
uprightness: He 1:8(LXX).†

εὐλάβεια.sd: properly, caution, i.e. (religiously) reverence (piety); by implication, dread (concretely)
εὐλάβεια.as:
εὐλάβεια, -ας, ἡ
(< εὐλαβής), [in LXX: Je 22:24 (דְּאָגָה), Pr 28:14, Wi 17:8 * ;]
1.caution, discretion (Soph., Plat., al.).
2. In later Gk. (Diod., Plut., al.), also reverence, godly fear: He 5:712:28.†
SYN.: v.s. δειλία (q.v.), φόβος (cf. Cremer, 387 f., 759; DB, ii. 222).

εὐαρεστέω.long: I give pleasure to, please (perhaps with the added idea of: rendering good service to).
εὐαρεστέω.as:
εὐαρεστέω, -ῶ
[in LXX chiefly for הָלַךְ hith., Ge 5:22, 24, Ps 25 (26):255 (56):13, al., Si 44:16 ;]
to be well pleasing: τ. θεῷ (LXX, ll. c.), He 11:5, 6. Pass., to be well pleased: c. dat., He 13:16.†

εὐλαβέομαι.long: I fear, am anxious, am cautious; I reverence.
εὐλαβέομαι.sd: to be circumspect, i.e. (by implication) to be apprehensive; religiously, to reverence
εὐλαβέομαι.as:
εὐλαβέομαι, -οῦμαι
[in LXX: Pr 24:28 (30:5), Na 1:7 (חָסָה), al., for 15 different Heb. words in all; also Si 7:2941:3, al. ;]
1.to be cautious, to beware: Ac 23:10 (Rec.; φοβηθείς, WH, RV).
2.to reverence: He 11:7 (cf. Cremer, 388).†

εὐπερίστατος.sd: well standing around, i.e. (a competitor) thwarting (a racer) in every direction (figuratively, of sin in genitive case)
εὐπερίστατος.der: from G2095 (εὖ) and a derivative of a presumed compound of G4012 (περί) and G2476 (ἵστημι);
εὐπερίστατος.as:
* εὐ-περί-στατος, -ον
(< εὖ, περιΐστημι),
of sins, readily besetting: He 12:1 (on form and sense of the word, v. Westc., in l.).†

εὐποιΐα.der: from a compound of G2095 (εὖ) and G4160 (ποιέω);
εὐποιΐα.as:
*† εὐ-ποιία (Rec. -ιΐα), -ας, ἡ
1.beneficence, doing good: He 13:16.
2.a benefit (FlJ, Ant., ii, 11, 2, al.).†

εὐπρέπεια.der: from a compound of G2095 (εὖ) and G4241 (πρέπω);
εὐπρέπεια.as:
εὐ-πρέπεια, -ας, ἡ
(< εὐπρεπής, comely), [in LXX for הָדָר, etc. ;]
goodly appearance, comeliness: Ja 1:11.†

εὐπειθής.as:
** εὐ-πειθής, ές,
(< εὖ, πείθομαι), [in LXX: IV Mac 12:6 AR* ;]
ready to obey, compliant: Ja 3:17.†

Εὐφράτης.long: the Euphrates, boundary river of the province Syria.
